solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be experienced, as should players?

definitions.meaning: to understand how things really stand, as a seasoned person does
players in a match ought literally to know what the score is

explanation.surface: A seasoned hand compared with sportsmen who ought to keep track of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the literal one: competitors should be aware of the current tally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be worldly and understand how a situation really works, which is what being experienced brings.

clue.text: Applicant seen, I'm only partly seek- ing promotion?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising or being promoted means the letters are read from bottom to top
only part of the run of words is taken, so the letters lie hidden within them

explanation.surface: An applicant notes that they are being seen as only half-heartedly after a better job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' hides EENIMON in 'seen, I'm only'; 'seeking promotion' turns it upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for a post or award, so like an applicant a candidate for selection.

clue.text: Documents blustering in conflict?

parts.note: a war is armed conflict
rants are blustering tirades

explanation.surface: Papers full of angry talk produced during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Warrants are official papers authorising an arrest, search or payment, so a kind of legal document.

clue.text: For example, straight bananas in a group

definitions.meaning: a straight is one example of a poker ...
a cluster of bananas growing together is called a ...

explanation.surface: An odd remark that straight bananas would be bunched together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straight' looks like an adjective for the fruit, but it is the poker holding of five cards in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the set of cards held is a hand; growers call each cluster of bananas a hand too.

clue.text: Athlete destroyed club

parts.note: something wrecked or ruined is said to be shot
a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A sportsman who has smashed his own golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field-event competitor who hurls a heavy metal ball, so a kind of track and field athlete.

clue.text: A little hideout, really strange

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone finds a small hiding place rather odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, describes something bizarre or unconventional, beyond normal bounds.

clue.text: Feeling passing after end of heart- ache

indicators.note: the movement word is placed after the single letter
the end of a word is its final letter, taken alone here

parts.note: motion is movement, the act of passing along

explanation.surface: A sentiment that comes once heartbreak has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy or grief, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: On the front line facing point of sword?

definitions.meaning: being ... means being where the real action and danger are
literally, someone facing the blade is at its sharp end

explanation.surface: A soldier in the forward trenches staring down an enemy's blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in the most demanding, exposed position, like troops in forward combat.

clue.text: Limitation placed on motor race, new, improved version

indicators.note: in a down entry, being placed on something puts it above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a rein is a check or restraint, as in keeping a rein on spending
motor is a common word for a car
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A restriction imposed on motor racing creates a fresh and better version of the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A reincarnation is a rebirth or a revived form of something, a new embodiment of an old thing.

clue.text: River cool for primate

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall in England
in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A river whose chilly waters suit a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American monkey, and monkeys are primates.

clue.text: Result has emerged the other way round?

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase swap places, putting the second word before the first

parts.note: to emerge is to come out, so has emerged is has come out

explanation.surface: A finding has turned up, but backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' swaps COME and OUT to give OUT before COME.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end result of a process.

clue.text: Dye painted on skin, Queen Eliza- beth's back viewed in the mirror?

indicators.note: a mirror image shows letters reversed, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of England

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Body art on a monarch seen reflected in a looking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' takes H from Elizabeth; 'viewed in the mirror' reverses ANNEH.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish plant dye used to decorate hands and feet with patterns.

clue.text: Old letter's recipient English, that man in Spain confused

indicators.note: confused says the combined letters are jumbled

parts.note: he refers to that man

explanation.surface: A bewildered Englishman abroad in Spain receives an old letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a container: 'confused' shuffles the pronoun and country together. The letter is St Paul's Epistle.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's Epistle to the Ephesians was addressed to the people of Ephesus, so an Ephesian received it.

clue.text: Romp with errand boy and artist

parts.note: a page is a boy who runs errands
J M W Turner was the English painter

explanation.surface: A frolic involving a messenger lad and a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a gripping book, and a romp is a lively, fast-moving story.

clue.text: Garment wasn't mended with paste

indicators.note: mended means repaired or put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing was repaired with glue rather than a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweatpants are loose jogging trousers, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Old South American currently visiting Colombia's outskirts

parts.note: in means in fashion, current

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An ancient Andean traveller is right now touring Colombian border areas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the people of the pre-Columbian empire centred on Peru.

clue.text: Close relationship, it's arising earlier

indicators.note: the turned piece comes before the affair
in a down entry, rising means the letters go upward, read in reverse

parts.note: a fling is a brief romantic relationship

explanation.surface: An intimate affair that started sooner than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb or 'near', but it is the weather sense: humid and airless. 'arising' and 'earlier' work only on the short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and airless, which is to say stifling.

clue.text: Range astoundingly large, pretty small initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Mountains that are amazingly big but rather small in scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.

clue.text: Standard, bargain vegetable

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a snip is a bargain in British usage

explanation.surface: An ordinary cheap vegetable at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root crop eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Ordinary cook earned tips

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rework them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A run-of-the-mill chef got gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a noun but is the verb rearranging EARNED and TIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull, plodding and unremarkable.

clue.text: One overcoming defeat, carrying on — resolve!

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming over something puts it above, so first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: carrying means the defeat word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: Someone who has got past a setback presses on with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' gives RONOUT, and in this down entry 'overcoming' puts the numeral on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out a problem is to settle or smooth it away, i.e. resolve it.

clue.text: Love dipping a sheep into stream

indicators.note: dipping a sheep means plunging it into liquid, so it goes inside the other piece
into marks the piece that receives the dipped sheep inside it

parts.note: to pour is to stream or flow
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sweetheart dunks a sheep into a brook, as at a sheep dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stream' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning flow; 'dipping into' places the animal inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is a lover, so someone's love.

clue.text: Second little animal, clean

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
a pup is a young animal

explanation.surface: A tiny creature is washed a moment later.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to wipe up spills, so to clean.

clue.text: Moving aloft — do this?

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: If you rise and drift up into the air, this is what you do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges ALOFT, and drifting aloft is to float, so the definition points back at the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something buoyed up and drifting in the air or on water is said to float.

clue.text: Sensitive cutting tool, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken, giving a word that is pronounced the same in British speech

parts.note: a saw is a toothed cutting tool

explanation.surface: A saw-like tool that is touchy when people listen.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British accents the tool and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore spot is tender and painful to touch, so sensitive.

clue.text: Square leg, target in game

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: Square leg is a cricket fielding position, made to sound like a game's target.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a fielding position on the leg side of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninepin is one of the skittles a bowler aims to knock down in the game of ninepins.

clue.text: Gold coin shimmering by old South American river

indicators.note: by means beside, so the last piece goes next

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: shimmering suggests flickering movement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A glinting gold coin found beside an ancient river in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is the great river of Venezuela.

clue.text: Office items I get, perhaps, designed to secure first bit of writing

indicators.note: securing means holding the other piece inside
designed means arranged or laid out afresh, so the letters are reshaped
takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone who draws up a plan to keep the first page of a manuscript in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges I GET PERHAPS; 'to secure' places W from 'first bit of writing' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperweights are heavy objects placed on desks to hold down loose sheets in an office.
